quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results, in line with management's expectations: revenue of $96.1 million from six license agreements (OTT, e-commerce, consumer electronics and Pay-TV customers) with a record 12 new customers added in the quarter; adjusted EBITDA $56.4 million, a 58.7% margin; $54.6 million cash from operations; $137.1 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities at quarter end. Non-GAAP operating expenses $40.2 million, down 6% from the prior quarter. Non-Pay-TV recurring revenue grew 54% year over year and is now nearly double the size of Pay-TV recurring revenue. CEO: renewal rate is over 90%; year-to-date revenue is about $201 million versus about $170 million at this point last year.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $96.1 million; adjusted EBITDA margin 58.7%; cash from operations $54.6 million; non-Pay-TV recurring revenue +54% YoY; 12 new customers

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: semiconductor revenue (hybrid bonding and other semiconductor IP licensing) was about $14.8 million in Q2 and about $48 million year to date, about 24% of first-half revenue, versus about $26 million for the whole of 2025 — 'our semiconductor business is headed in a great direction'.
quarterly_data.figure: semiconductor revenue ~$14.8 million in Q2; ~$48 million year to date (~24%); ~$26 million full-year 2025

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 guidance reiterated: revenue $395 million to $435 million; operating expenses $184 million to $192 million; interest expense $34 million to $36 million; other income $5.5 million to $6.5 million; adjusted EBITDA margin approximately 55%; non-GAAP tax rate 21%; capital expenditures approximately $2 million. CFO: full-year cash from operations still about $150 million, with Q3 fairly modest and a resurgence in Q4; year-end cash targeted at about $100 million. quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenue $395 million to $435 million; opex $184 million to $192 million; adjusted EBITDA margin ~55%; capex ~$2 million; cash from operations ~$150 million

quarterly_data.signal: Long-term targets raised: the annual revenue target goes to $600 million from $500 million, driven by the semiconductor market. The long-term semiconductor opportunity is raised to $200 million annually from the previously estimated $100 million, on broader and faster adoption of hybrid bonding; CEO: achievable in about five years (the long-range planning horizon). The long-term media target is unchanged at $400 million annually. CEO: e-commerce licensing could grow over the long term to a size similar to consumer electronics, which has been approximately 10% of total revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: long-term revenue target $600 million (from $500 million); semiconductor $200 million annually (from $100 million) in about five years; media $400 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO view on hybrid-bonding adoption: hybrid bonding has become a critical enabler of next-generation chip architectures (density, performance, thermal management). AMD started shipping hybrid-bonded logic devices in 2022; Apple, Intel and Broadcom all have products ramping into production using hybrid bonding. He believes hybrid bonding will be a requirement in HBM with 20 or more layers, if not sooner, and in NAND as layer counts approach 400, with the big three memory players all ramping to get there. Leading foundries, memory companies and OSATs are planning to spend approximately $125 billion in the near term on advanced packaging including hybrid bonding — 'we know broad adoption of hybrid bonding is coming because the capital equipment required is being ordered.' Hyperscalers 'are semiconductor companies now', differentiating with their own chips, which he expects to create additional opportunity. He puts the semiconductor market at over $1.5 trillion this year.
quarterly_data.figure: HBM with 20 or more layers; NAND approaching 400 layers; ~$125 billion near-term advanced-packaging spend; semiconductor market over $1.5 trillion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: 3D NAND leader SanDisk is an Adeia customer and began using hybrid bonding for NAND in 2023.
CEO: 3D NAND leader Kioxia is an Adeia customer and began using hybrid bonding for NAND in 2023.

CEO on RapidCool (Adeia's chip thermal-management technology): it is plug-and-play in current data centers and uses existing equipment; he sees it as an important element of relicensing efforts with the memory players and in logic, licensed on a portfolio-wide basis — 'hybrid bonding is kind of now'.

Customer Google: one of the most significant Q2 license agreements was a multiyear renewal with Google for access to Adeia's media portfolio; Google has been a customer for approximately 15 years, and CEO cites YouTube TV's subscriber growth. With the Disney agreement signed last year (including Hulu + Live TV), Adeia counts two of the largest virtual MVPD platforms as customers.
quarterly_data.figure: multiyear renewal; customer for approximately 15 years

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Microsoft: CEO lists a license agreement with Microsoft among those closed in the first half of 2026 (alongside AMD, Google and RPX).

Customer RPX: Q2 multiyear, term-based license with RPX, a patent risk solutions company, covering 10 participating member companies in a single agreement with a term license to Adeia's media portfolio of approximately 10,900 patent assets, driven by e-commerce technologies. CEO: the deal structure can potentially be replicated; the first e-commerce license came at the end of 2024 and e-commerce is now a meaningful contributor. Other Q2 deals: a new multiyear license with L'Oreal, a new multiyear license with a streaming documentary provider, and renewals with a European Pay-TV provider and a Japanese consumer electronics manufacturer.

IP portfolio: six tuck-in portfolio acquisitions in Q2 for $9.5 million, focused on e-commerce, OTT and imaging; the portfolio grew to over 14,250 patent assets, up approximately 4% from Q1. CEO: semiconductor portfolios are also being evaluated for acquisition. Adeia filed patent infringement claims against Fubo asserting four media patents after failing to reach license terms; CEO says the Pay-TV litigation creates headwinds and its timing is hard to predict.
quarterly_data.figure: six acquisitions for $9.5 million; over 14,250 patent assets (+~4% QoQ); four patents asserted against Fubo

connects_to.relationship: multi-year semiconductor IP license (hybrid bonding / advanced packaging patents)
